title: Grading the Chicago Bears vs. the New England Patriots
text: Grading the Chicago Bears vs. the New England Patriots Here’s how we graded the Bears’ against the Patriots on Thursday Night Football. In a heavy fight between two 4-2 teams, the Bears and Patriots came down to the wire. In a heavy fight between two 4-2 teams, the Bears and Patriots came down to the wire. Here’s how we graded the Bears’ against the Patriots on Thursday Night Football. That’s 20 first-half points for the second week in a row, and another efficient game where Caleb Williams moved the ball consistently. Against a New England team that prides itself on defense under head coach Mike Vrabel, the Bears put up over 400 yards of offense, scored three touchdowns and moved the ball in key moments. It wasn’t always pretty.The Bears stalled a bit in the third quarter, giving New England a chance to stay on a roll. On a key fourth and two, the Bears moved the chains in the fourth. They went to Luther Burden III and he tore into the Patriots’ defense. This was not a banner day for the defense.The elephant in the room was the last play before halftime, which ended up being a critical score that gave the Patriots’ life. Drake Maye is a great quarterback. He’s coming into his own, and did so at the expense of the Bears’ defense. The Bears couldn’t pressure the Patriots, who were down two starting guards.That last play of the first half was just inexcusable. Their B grade is getting bumped down to a C+ because of it. He leads the offense, takes what’s given to him, evades pressure and put the ball into the end zone. In the fourth quarter, Williams just ripped a third down, gotta-have-it through to Rome Odunze.It was impressive as it was needed. He went over 300 yards passing and never gave New England a chance to win the game. His only bad play was taking a bad sack, but Cairo Santos bailed him out. Jaylon JohnsonEarlier in the game, he was juked by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.Maye is pretty athletic, but it’s not like Johnson was trying to bring Michael Vick in his prime down to the turf. On that last play of the half, his half-hearted tackle attempt helped the Patriots add a touchdown that helped the Patriots get a score that was critical in the fourth quarter.
